RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, December 9, 2010/Agrahayana 18, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Culture; External
Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation; Overseas
Indian Affairs; Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel,
Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Space;
Tourism; Urban Development;
Water Resources; Youth Affairs
and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
132
Districts affected by arsenic
in ground water
*421. SHRIMA TI KUSUM RAI: Will
the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of districts of the country
which are affected by presence of arsenic
and other heavy metals in ground water,
State-wise;
(b) whether Government is aware that
in these districts which are affected by
arsenic and other heavy metals, large number
of children are born totally blind;
(c) if so, the number of such children,
State-wise; and
(d) the details of programmes being run
by the Ministry for treatment of heavy
metals from ground water, State-wise?
Selection of CMDs of PSUs
*422. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether selection of CMDs of PSUs
is monitored by any designated authority
or it is left to the discretion of the concerned
Ministry for processing the
recommendations of the Public Enterprises
Selection Board till its final approval by
the Appointments Committee of the
Cabinet;
(b) the number of Central PSUs which
were without regular CMD's as on
30 September, 2010; and
(c) whether the existing selection
procedure for Board level functionaries
needs more professional orientation?

133
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Proposals for privatisation of printing
presses
*423. SHRI RUDRA NARAY AN
PANY: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there are other schemes and
programmes monitored and implemented
by the Ministry besides the Jawaharlal
Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there are some printing
presses under the Ministry;
(d) whether it is a fact that proposals
for privatisation of these printing presses
are under consideration; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Groups in Kashmir seeking American
intervention
†*424. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VY AS:
Will the Minister of EXTERAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether some groups in Kashmir
are seeking American intervention;
(b) whether some of them are also
preparing to give a signed memorandum to
the American President;
(c) Government's approach towards
these activities;
(d) whether any action has been taken
considering it to be an interference in
internal affairs of the country; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Irrigation potential
*425. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of W ATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether against the target of creation
of irrigation potential of 10 million hectare
in four years, i.e. from 2005-06 to 2008-
09, only 7.31 million hectare has been
created upto March, 2009;
(b) whether the target for creation of
irrigation potential during the years
2009-10 and 2010-11 is stated to be 3.50
million hectare only; and
(c) whether above statistics show
woeful neglect of irrigation which is one of
the six components for development of
rural infrastructure under Bharat Nirman?
Construction of big dams in
Arunachal Pradesh
*426. SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite being
World's number one large dam builder, USA
is actually decommissioning, literally
removing some of its dams, after a reality
check about their benefit;
(b) whether such case studies have been
conducted before giving green signal for the
construction of big dams in Arunachal
Pradesh;
(c) if so, the details of such studies;
(d) whether Government would move
for rethinking of the proposed construction
of big dams particularly in Arunachal

134
Pradesh considering the cost benefit
analysis and environmental impact of
hydro power dams and also economic value
of the free flow of rivers; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Pune Metro Project
*427. SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has given in
principle sanction to Pune Metro Project;
(b) the status of the Project at present;
and
(c) the reasons for Government delaying
clearance to the Project?
Initiative for flood control and
management
*428. SHRI  NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR: Will the Minister of W ATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the initiative undertaken and
responsibilities shared by Government in
flood control and management;
(b) whether breach of dams, canals and
embankments have been reported in various
States, including Gujarat State, during the
recent monsoon;
(c) if so, the details thereof along with
the funds granted for their repair and
maintenance, State-wise; and
(d) the steps taken by Government for
prevention of flooding downstream and
mitigating loss of life and property in river
basins?
Proposals from Tamil Nadu
*429. SHRI P AUL MANOJ
PANDIAN: Will the Minister of
TOURISM be pleased to state whether
Government would obtain proposals from
the State Government of Tamil Nadu to
declare Papahasam Dam, Agasthiyar Falls
and Kutralam in Tirunelveli district as
tourism spots and allocate funds for the
development of the above tourist places?
Changes in syllabus for CSE
*430. SHRI RANJITSINH
VIJAYSINH MOHITE-PATIL: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has allowed
UPSC to change the structure of syllabus
for All India Civil Services Examination;
(b) the reasons leading to the change in
the existing structure of the preliminary
examination of All India Civil Services; and
(c) whether the change in the structure
of Preliminary Examination has been made
keeping in view the interest of regional/
rural candidates?
Building modern stadia
*431. SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI: Will
the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
build modern stadia for encouraging youth
to participate in sports in rural areas of the
country during the current financial year;
(b) if so, the details in this regard, State-
wise;
(c) the details of stadia constructed
during the current Five Year Plan in various
States so far; and

135
(d) the details of funds allocated by
Government for the development of sports
during the Eleventh Five Y ear Plan, so far,
year-wise, particularly to Chhattisgarh?
Study of Chinese projects on
Brahmaputra river
*432. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has made any
study of construction projects being
planned/executed along the Brahmaputra
river in the Tibet region by China as a part
of its South North Water Diversion Project;
(b) if so, based on Government's
assessment, the likely reduction in water
flow to the river in India and its projected
impact on the water availability in the
North Eastern States as a consequence; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
raise India's concerns with China in this
regard?
Legal framework for protection of
monuments
*433. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the existing legal framework for
protection of monuments in the country;
(b) the details of the unprotected
monuments in the country, State-wise;
(c) the details of financial assistance
given to the States during the last two years
for preservation of unprotected
monuments along with the details of
amount spent during the last two years
and the current year, monument-wise;
(d) whether Government proposes to
formulate a comprehensive legislation for
conservation and protection of all
monuments in the country; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Expectations met from CWG 2010
*434. SHRI MANI SHANKAR
AIYAR: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Commonwealth Games
2010, measured up to the spectacular
success he had hoped for in terms of macro
and micro-management, budget, timely
submission of plans and completion of
projects, tourist arrivals, pojection of India's
image in the domestic media and abroad,
and returns on investment made in financial
and broader terms; and
(b) whether he would ensure that bids
for mega international sports events, such
as the Asiad and the Olympics, are not
made till organized sports facilities reach
the bulk of our children and youth through
the Panchayat Y uva Khel aur Krida
Abhiyan?
Agreements signed during the visit  of
American President
†*435. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of agreements signed
between India and America during American
President's recent India visit, and the names
of sectors to be benefited therefrom in India;
(b) the salient features of pollution-free
energy agreement between India and
America and the amount of investment to
be made in the next five years to promote
pollution-free energy; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

136
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) the names of States, where clean
energy research and development centres
would be established under this scheme?
Results of Indo-Pak talks
*436. SHRI TARIQ ANW AR: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India-Pak
talks have not yielded positive results;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that India
has been at the receiving end during the
talks; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Production of nuclear weapon by
Pakistan
†*437. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken
notice of the report of American Nuclear
Monitoring Institute, 'The Institute for
Science and International Security,'
according to which the entire assembly line
of cooling towers in Pakistan's Khushab
third reactor is ready whereby Pakistan
would step up plutonium production for
manufacturing nuclear weapons;
(b) whether it is a fact that Pakistan has
70 to 90 nuclear weapons;
(c) whether it is also a fact that all the
defence preparedness of Pakistan could be
used against India; and
(d) if so, the action being taken by
Government in this regard?
Cases pending with CBI
*438. SHRI BALWINDER SINGH
BHUNDER: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases initiated by CBI
against bureaucrats of the level of Joint
Secretary and above, and pending at
present;
(b) the number out of them, in which
charge-sheets have been filed within the
stipulated period and the number in which
extension of time has been sought from the
designated courts; and
(c) the date from which the oldest case
is pending and the steps being taken to
expedite the cases, particularly those
pending for over five years?
Pending applications for grant-in-aid
scheme of Tamil Nadu
*439. SHRIMATI V ASANTHI
STANLEY: Will the Minister of SOCIAL
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of applications
pending for release of grant-in-aid under
various categories in the Ministry from
Tamil Nadu;
(b) the total value of this grant for these
schemes;
(c) by when these applications would
be cleared;
(d) the reasons for the delay in clearing
the pending applications; and
(e) whether it is also a fact that there is
no proper monitoring of pending cases in
the Ministry and the steps taken to
improve the situation?

137
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 3rd December, 2010 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 12, 1932 (Saka)
Access to toilets in rural/urban India
*440. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether more than 6.5 crore
households do not have access to toilets in
rural and urban India;
(b) if so, the steps being taken and
whether schemes implemented in this regard
are effective; and
(c) the reasons why only 45 per cent
subsidy is provided under Integrated Low
Cost Sanitation Scheme (ILCSS) to the
Economically Weaker Sections?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Prime Minister :—
Atomic Energy :—
Culture : 433,
External Affairs : 424, 432, 435, 436, 437,
Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation : 440,
Overseas Indian Affairs :—

Planning :—

Space :—
Tourism : 429,
Urban Development : 423, 427,
Water Resources : 421, 425, 426, 428,
Youth Affairs and Sports : 431, 434.
